_provenance.note: No NIST ACVP reference vector exists for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256/SHA512 (checked 2026-08-28, WS-7: the NIST reference set at gen-val/json-files/PBKDF-1.0 only covers SHA2-224, which this engine's CKM_PKCS5_PBKD2 does not implement — only SHA256/384/512 PRFs are dispatched). Values independently computed with Node's crypto (OpenSSL) module; the same oracle reproduces RFC 6070's SHA-1 vectors exactly (RFC 6070 itself is SHA-1-only, not cross-engine-verifiable here). Self-consistency tier, not NIST ACVP or a published standard's own KAT. UPDATE 2026-09-26: the PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 cases moved to pbkdf2_rfc7914_test.json, which takes them from RFC 7914 section 11 (a published consensus RFC) instead of Node/OpenSSL output. This file now holds only the PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 cases, which no standard publishes, so they stay self-generated and are labelled that way.
